newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ aims to keep div payout ratio.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ aims to keep div payout ratio.

text.p: Australia and New Zelanad Banking Corp Ltd (ANZ) said on Wednesday it aimed to keep its dividend payout ratio at about 55 percent and that the bank planned to use retained earnings to fund future growth.

"The main criteria will be our capital needs and we see that as giving the capital, without going to shareholders, to continue to grow this business," chairman Charles Goode told the bank's annual meeting. "I think it (dividend payout ratio) will stay much the same for this bank, we have growth opportunities."
"We have got growth opportunities, internationally in particular," he said.

Goode was responding to a question from the Australian shareholders Association, which asked if the bank could increase its payout ratio to match the Commonwealth bank of Australia's 78 percent ratio.

Goode confirmed that ANZ's capital adequacy ratio of 6.7 percent on tier one capital was well above the prudential norms, but he said ANZ wanted to keep this ratio at between 6.5 and seven percent to maintain its AA credit rating.
"We aim to be 6.5 to seven percent, so we are about where we wish to be for a good utilisation of capital," Goode said.
ANZ paid a total dividend of 42 cents a share in the year to September 30, 1996. It reported earnings per share of 76.3 cents in the 1995/96 year.
